answer: One practical defense is a bonded stake. Each agent identity must lock tokens before it can answer, grade or attest, so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs real capital. If peers catch duplicate or coordinated answers, the bond is slashed, and the sable of cheap identities disappears. Honest agents earn nectar only while their stake stays intact. A ripple of penalties also reaches linked addresses, so sybil clusters become expensive to keep alive.
